name.text: Calculating a missing probability and cumulative probability for a discrete distribution

questiontext.text:
Wanjiru runs a kiosk and records the number of items (\(X\)) a customer buys per visit. From her records, she estimates the probability distribution below, but one entry was accidentally erased.

\(X\) (Items bought) 0 1 2 3 4
\(P(X = x)\) {@p0@} {@p1@} ? {@p3@} {@p4@}

a) For the table to represent a valid Probability Distribution Function (PDF), the sum of all probabilities must equal exactly 1. Calculate the missing probability.

\(P(X = 2) =\) [[input:ans1]]

[[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

b) Calculate the probability that a randomly selected customer buys at least 2 items.

\(P =\) [[input:ans2]]

[[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution:

Part a: Finding the missing probability
A discrete probability distribution is only valid if the sum of all probabilities equals exactly 1.

\( \displaystyle \sum P(X=x) = 1 \)

\( P(X=0) + P(X=1) + P(X=2) + P(X=3) + P(X=4) = 1 \)

\( {@p0@} + {@p1@} + P(X=2) + {@p3@} + {@p4@} = 1 \)

\( {@p0 + p1 + p3 + p4@} + P(X=2) = 1 \)

\( P(X=2) = 1 - {@p0 + p1 + p3 + p4@} \)

\( \displaystyle \boxed{ P(X=2) = {@ta1@} } \)

Part b: Cumulative Probability
The phrase "at least 2" means the customer buys 2, 3, or 4 items. We find this by summing the relevant probabilities from the table:

\( \displaystyle P(X \ge 2) = P(X=2) + P(X=3) + P(X=4) \)

\( \displaystyle P(X \ge 2) = {@ta1@} + {@p3@} + {@p4@} \)

\( \displaystyle \boxed{ P(X \ge 2) = {@ta2@} } \)

questiondescription.text:
Discrete Probability (Validating PDF and Cumulative Probability)

Grade 11 CBE: Calculating a missing probability to ensure a valid PDF sum of 1, and calculating a cumulative 'at least' probability.

prtcorrect.text: Correct answer, well done.

prtpartiallycorrect.text: Your answer is partially correct.

prtincorrect.text: Incorrect answer.

truefeedback.text: Correct. You successfully subtracted the known probabilities from 1 to complete the valid PDF.

falsefeedback.text: Incorrect. Remember that the sum of all probabilities in a valid distribution must equal exactly 1. Add up the probabilities for X=0, 1, 3, and 4, then subtract that total from 1.

truefeedback.text: Excellent. You correctly summed the probabilities for \(X \ge 2\).

node.description: Check if they forgot to include P(X=2)

truefeedback.text: The symbol \(\ge\) means "greater than or equal to". You summed \(P(X=3)\) and \(P(X=4)\), but you forgot to include your result for \(P(X=2)\).

falsefeedback.text: Incorrect. To find \(P(X \ge 2)\), you must add together the individual probabilities for \(X=2\), \(X=3\), and \(X=4\).
